title: GET /delete/<id> reports success for a post that does not exist
property: deleting a nonexistent (or already deleted) post does not report 'Post Deleted' with status 1; it is a 404 or status 0
input: logged in, no posts, GET /delete/1 (or a second GET /delete/1 after deleting post 1)
expected: 404 or JSON status 0 (error), since nothing was deleted
actual: 200 {"message": "Post Deleted", "status": 1} and flash 'The entry was deleted.'
evidence: The handler's own result dict defaults to {status: 0, message: 'Error'} and sets status 1 'Post Deleted' unconditionally after query.delete(), ignoring the returned row count. REST convention: deleting an unknown id gives 404, and a repeat delete is 404.
